chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a boy has been born to me, so what should I name him?' He said: 'Name him with the name most beloved to me, Hamza.'
ai.seo_question: What is the most beloved name to the Prophet according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys the Prophet’s preference for the name Hamza, highlighting the virtue of the Prophet’s uncle and the significance of naming children after noble figures. This reflects the Shia emphasis on selecting names that carry spiritual weight and connect the child to the Ahl al-Bayt and early Islamic leadership. The recommendation underscores the belief that a name influences identity and destiny within the Islamic tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! A boy has been born for me, so what is that I should name him with?’ He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘By the most beloved of the names to me<sup>saww</sup>, Hamza’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a man came to the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, a son is born to me. What must I name him?’
He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Name him with the name which is most beloved to Hamzah.’”
